name: RR Opague
classification_notes: Circular 'O' forms and strongly horizontal apertures create a hard, even rhythm at low contrast. Postmodern sensibility referencing nineteenth-century grotesques including Bernard Brothers & Spindler's Lining Gothic nº82 and Bauer's Venus.
summary: A postmodern geometric sans in nine weights with italics, drawing on historical grotesque precedents with contemporary precision.
description: Opague is shaped by a circular 'O' and enforced horizontal lines through its apertures and midpoints, giving it a hard, even typographic colour. Nine weights run from Thin to Black, each with a matching 15° italic, with a variable font included. Over 1000 glyphs per style cover Latin, Cyrillic and Greek across 280+ languages, with case-sensitive punctuation, multiple figure sets and ten stylistic sets.
foundry_blurb: Rüdiger describes Opague as a synthetically distilled postmodern geometric sans, its character shaped by a circular O and horizontal lines through the apertures and middle height. A subdued palette and near-anonymous quality let it dominate at display scale or recede into interface copy without losing authority. The variable font expands the 18-style static family into an almost infinite range of intermediate options.

name: RR Repose
classification_notes: Uppercase-only geometric sans at a single light weight, built around fixed-width proportional logic where O equals double H equals double I. Not a text face – designed exclusively for large-scale display. Six styles derived from rounding and spacing choices rather than a weight range.
summary: Uppercase-only geometric display sans in six rounding and spacing variations, built for large-scale headline use.
description: Repose is an uppercase-only light sans in six styles derived from three corner-rounding levels – fully rounded, inside corners only, no rounding – crossed with two spacing approaches. Prop uses proportional kerning for tight, elegant setting; Quad abandons kerning for a fixed-width quadrospace that reads with deliberate technical awkwardness at scale. Proportions are grounded in a simple fixed-width logic where O is double H is double I.
foundry_blurb: Rüdiger designed Repose to be used big and ostentatiously: spread across movie titles, record covers, building-sized banners and haughty headlines. The Quad sub-collection forgoes kerning in favour of simplicity and a technical awkwardness; Prop maintains the same dynamic proportions with kerning for tighter, more modest elegance. Both sub-collections cover 280+ languages across Latin and Cyrillic.
